security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick, URL, and prose false positives. The real risks are intentional RunComfy CLI execution, outbound requests to RunComfy with user content, generated file downloads, and persistent API token storage.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running RunComfy commands, keep arguments fixed, and avoid passing unreviewed shell fragments.
Warn users before sending confidential prompts, reference images, masks, videos, or URLs to RunComfy services.
Document token revocation, keep mode 0600, and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI or short-lived environments.
Pin the RunComfy CLI version and avoid global installation when a project-local or ephemeral command is enough.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast image drafts without rewriting prompts for each test. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RunComfy Flux 2 Klein workflows.
actual_capabilities: Invokes RunComfy Flux 2 Klein 4B for fast concept images.
Invokes RunComfy Flux 2 Klein 9B for polished images.
Documents width, height, step count, and prompt fields.
Supports up to four reference images when the endpoint accepts them.
Guides subject-first prompts for stronger image results.
Explains when to choose Flux 2 Pro, Seedream 5, or GPT Image 2.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a working RunComfy account.
Sends prompts and optional asset URLs to RunComfy services.
Does not run Flux 2 Klein locally or self-host models.
Works best within the documented prompt, aspect ratio, and resolution limits.

use_cases.title: Create rapid product concepts
use_cases.description: Use the 4B variant to explore product visuals quickly before selecting a final direction.

use_cases.title: Polish campaign imagery
use_cases.description: Move selected concepts to the 9B variant for sharper details and consistent visual style.

use_cases.title: Align visuals with references
use_cases.description: Use aligned reference images to guide composition, lighting, and brand style across assets.

prompt_templates.title: Start a fast concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a quick draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein 4B to create a fast concept image for [subject]. Keep the prompt direct and save it to [output folder].

prompt_templates.title: Refine a product image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for sharper commercial output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein 9B to generate a polished product image of [product]. Include lighting, camera, background, dimensions, and step count.

prompt_templates.title: Match brand references
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein with these reference images: [paths or URLs]. Preserve the style, then change [specific element] for [campaign goal].

prompt_templates.title: Plan live iteration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for art direction sessions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run three Flux 2 Klein 4B variations for [scene], compare results, then produce one final 9B version with the strongest composition.

output_examples.input: Create a fast concept for a ceramic mug on a bright kitchen counter.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a subject-first image prompt, selects the fast 4B variant, and saves a concept image for review.

output_examples.input: Make a polished wide poster image for a new running shoe campaign.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the 9B variant, uses poster dimensions within limits, and returns a polished generated image file.

output_examples.input: Use three brand references to create a matching bottle image.
output_examples.output: The skill keeps the references stylistically aligned and describes what should stay fixed and what should change.

best_practices: Start with 4B for exploration, then use 9B for final image quality.
Keep prompts subject-first with clear scene, style, lighting, and camera details.
Use only aligned reference images so the model receives a consistent visual target.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential prompts or private reference images without approval.
Do not exceed the documented prompt length, resolution, or aspect ratio limits.
Do not mix unrelated visual styles across reference images in one request.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to call RunComfy hosted model endpoints.

faq.question: Which variant should I use first?
faq.answer: Use 4B for fast exploration and 9B when you are ready to polish the image.

faq.question: Can I use reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents reference image support when the RunComfy endpoint accepts those fields.

faq.question: Does it support high resolution output?
faq.answer: It is designed around the documented Flux 2 Klein limits, not native 4K generation.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated outputs into the output directory passed by the user.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: Prompts, model inputs, and optional asset URLs are sent to RunComfy services during generation.
